newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Underemployment rife as Vietnam's population booms.
newsitem.headline: Underemployment rife as Vietnam's population booms.

text.p: A survey into employment levels in Vietnam has shown that more than a quarter of the communist country's fast expanding rural workforce had jobs for only part of the year during 1996.
The official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) released details late on Tuesday of a recent Labour Ministry survey showing that rural underemployment last year affected 27.65 percent of people aged over 15.
Urban unemployment was meanwhile rated at 5.88 percent among working age people compared with 6.08 percent in 1994, although a precise definition of "working age" was not provided.
Around 80 percent of Vietnam's 77 million population live in rural areas, where many have scarce work between the planting of crops and harvesting.
The VNA report said the survey showed that rural underemployment rates had dropped since 1994, although the comparative figures provided were unclear.
Providing employment for Vietnam's fast expanding population is a significant problem for the government in Hanoi.

Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has recently called for the mobilisation of the national workforce through compulsory labour and other schemes, partly as a means of tackling the problem through the creation of vast infrastructure projects.
According to a separate report in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper three people are born every minute -- equivalent in terms of population size to one new province each year.

International agencies say population growth is running at around 2.0 percent per annum -- despite a strict government policy allowing only two children per family -- requiring the creation of 1.5 million new jobs each year.
VNA said the Labour Ministry survey was based on sample interviews with 125,090 households.
